commitResults.messageTitle: Level 0: Rename chatbot to HSE and implement greet/exit
Level 1 and 2: Echo commands and add task list
Level 4:Add todo deadline and event tasks
Add command objects for application actions
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce an abstract Command contract and concrete commands for listing, finding, adding, marking, unmarking, deleting, invalid input, and exit behavior.

Teach Parser to construct the matching command object, then simplify HSE.run() into a coordination loop that reads input through Ui, executes the parsed command, and exits through Command.isExit(). Ui now supplies command input and divider output.

This replaces HSE's command switch and operation-specific helpers with polymorphic command behavior while preserving the existing task storage and error messages.

Move application code beneath the hse namespace while keeping src/main/java as the source root.\n\nSeparate application coordination, commands, parsing, storage, tasks, and console UI into hse, hse.command, hse.parser, hse.storage, hse.task, and hse.ui. Add package declarations and explicit imports without changing application behavior.
Set the application plugin main class to hse.HSE so Gradle launches the packaged application entry point.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit coverage for parsing and date matching
commitResults.messageBody: Add Parser tests for one-based index conversion and invalid task numbers. Add TaskList tests for matching deadline/event dates, excluding todos, and returning empty results when nothing matches.

The task model exposes public constructors and behavior methods without
explaining their intended contracts.

Add JavaDoc for task types, creation, completion changes, date matching,
and display output so callers can understand each public API without
reading its implementation.

Several control statements use one-line bodies and some task classes
have inconsistent whitespace. These forms make later edits easier to
misread and do not meet the project convention.

Use braced control bodies and consistent spacing throughout the affected
classes. This keeps behavior unchanged while making future changes safer
to review.

Future work needs a clear project-level entry point for the Java and Git
conventions.

Link the local convention guides from AGENTS.md so agents apply them
whenever they edit code or create commits.

The project needs reusable guidance for the Java conventions required by
the course.

Add a concise local skill covering naming, layout, imports, braces, and
JavaDoc expectations for future Java changes.

Future commits need consistent subjects and useful explanatory bodies.

Add a local skill that records the required commit-message and commit
scope conventions.

The find command searches dates, which does not meet the Level 9
requirement to find task descriptions by keyword.

Search task descriptions for the requested keyword and display matching
tasks in their original order. Reject an empty keyword and add tests for
matching and non-matching searches.

Level 9 repurposes find for keyword searches, leaving the existing
date-search helpers unreachable from the command line.

Add finddate DATE to preserve the Level 8 stretch feature without
conflicting with find KEYWORD. Cover parser recognition with a JUnit test.
